'''Hrvoje Tkalčić''' {{Post-nominals|country=AUS|FAA}} (English pronunciation: hur-VOY-eh  tuh-KAL-cheech) (born 3 February 1970) is an Australian and Croatian [[Geophysics|geophysicist]] and Professor E2 at the [[Australian National University]] in [[Canberra]].<ref name="WHO-01">[https://tkojetko.irb.hr/en/znanstvenikDetalji.php?sifznan=9151 Who is Who in Croatian Science: Hrvoje Tkalčić]. Retrieved 24 February 2018.</ref>

== Biography ==
Hrvoje Tkalčić studied physics and geophysics at the [[Faculty of Science, University of Zagreb|University of Zagreb (Faculty of Science)]], from which he gained a Diploma of [[Engineering]] in [[Physics]] degree (speciality in Geophysics with [[meteorology]]) in 1996. He continued his postgraduate study at the [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California at Berkeley]] in the Department of [[Earth science|Earth]] and [[Planetary Science]], and defended a [[PhD thesis]] entitled ''Study of deep Earth structure using seismic body waves'' in 2001.<ref>[https://tkojetko.irb.hr/en/znanstvenikDetalji.php?sifznan=9151&podaci=izobrazba Who is Who in Croatian Science: Hrvoje Tkalčić – Education]. Retrieved 24 February 2018.</ref>
He was employed as a [[research assistant]] at the UC Berkeley Seismological Laboratory (1997&ndash;2001), as a postdoctoral fellow at the Institute of Geophysics and Planetary Physics of the [[University of California, San Diego|University of California San Diego]] (2002&ndash;2003), and as a postdoctoral researcher at [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] in [[Livermore, California]] (2003&ndash;2006). In 2006, he began a continuing position as Scientist in the Seismology group at Multimax, Inc., in [[Emeryville, California]]. From January 2007 until April 2013, he was a [[Fellow]] at the Research School of Earth Sciences (RSES) of the Australian National University (ANU), Canberra, Australia. From April 2013 until December 2018, he was a Senior Fellow and [[associate professor]] in [[Seismology]] and [[Mathematical Geophysics]] at RSES, ANU. He was Head of Seismology and Mathematical Geophysics from January 2017 to April 2021 and Professor E1 from January 2019 to June 2023. He has been Head of the Geophysics Area since April 2021 and Professor E2 since June 2023.<ref>[https://tkojetko.irb.hr/en/znanstvenikDetalji.php?sifznan=9151&podaci=zaposlenja Who is Who in Croatian Science: Hrvoje Tkalčić – Employment]. Retrieved 24 February 2018.</ref>

He has published 130 papers in peer-review journals in the field of seismology and mathematical geophysics,<ref>[https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Hrvoje_Tkalcic Australian National University, Canberra – ResearchGate: Hrvoje Tkalčić] Retrieved 4 December 2020.</ref> and an academic book on the Earth's inner core.<ref>[http://admin.cambridge.org/uy/academic/subjects/earth-and-environmental-science/solid-earth-geophysics/earths-inner-core-revealed-observational-seismology?format=HB#YOkkoEZ0XhuUlFKP.97 Cambridge University Press – The Earth's Inner Core]. Retrieved 4 December 2020.</ref> His primary research interests involve studying Earth's structure and dynamics using state-of-the-art seismological techniques, with the main focus on the Earth's core and the lowermost mantle, and developing new techniques for imaging Earth's interior, including both seismic and correlation wavefield. Other interests include studying the physics of tectonic and volcanic earthquakes by means of waveform modelling and improving volumetric raypath coverage of the Earth's interior through the installation of seismic instruments in remote parts of the planet, including on the ocean bottom.<ref>[https://tkojetko.irb.hr/znanstvenikDetalji.php?sifznan=9151&podaci=znanstveniinteresi Tko je tko u hrvatskoj znanosti: Hrvoje Tkalčić – Znanstveni interesi] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160924153522/https://tkojetko.irb.hr/znanstvenikDetalji.php?sifznan=9151&podaci=znanstveniinteresi |date=24 September 2016}}. {{in lang|hr}} Retrieved 4 December 2020.</ref><ref>[https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Hrvoje_Tkalcic Australian National University – Research School of Earth Sciences: : Hrvoje Tkalčić]. Retrieved 4 December 2020.</ref>

He participated in a number of scientific field campaigns to establish temporary seismic networks in remote parts of Australia and the Southern Ocean. The main objective has been to image the structure of the [[Internal structure of Earth|Earth's interior]] using [[seismic tomography]] and other imaging techniques. He actively participates in special sessions at a number of international geophysical conferences.<ref name="HT-Vitae">[http://rses.anu.edu.au/~hrvoje/HT_Vitae_web.pdf The Australian National University – Research School of Earth Sciences: Hrvoje Tkalčić, Curriculum Vitae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180313170540/http://rses.anu.edu.au/~hrvoje/HT_Vitae_web.pdf |date=13 March 2018 }}. Retrieved 24 February 2018.</ref> He is a member of the [[American Geophysical Union]] and [[Seismological Society of America]],<ref>[https://tkojetko.irb.hr/znanstvenikDetalji.php?sifznan=9151&podaci=clanstva Tko je tko u hrvatskoj znanosti: Hrvoje Tkalčić – Članstva] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911225655/https://tkojetko.irb.hr/znanstvenikDetalji.php?sifznan=9151&podaci=clanstva |date=11 September 2018 }}. {{in lang|hr}} Retrieved 24 February 2018.</ref>  a Fellow of the [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]], and a Fellow of the [[Royal Astronomical Society|Royal Astronomical Society, London]]. He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Geophysical Union]] and a Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]]. He has been serving on the editorial board of the journals ''[[Physics of the Earth and Planetary Interiors]]'', ''[[Scientific Reports]]'' and ''Geofizika''. He was a member of the [[Australian Research Council]] College of Experts and New Zealand [[Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment]] College of Assessors and on the committees of the American Geophysical Union and the Australian Academy of Science. He is Director of Warramunga Seismic and Infrasound Research Station in [[Northern Territory, Australia]].<ref name="HT-Vitae"/> In 2025, he was awarded an [[Australian Laureate Fellowship]] for the program "Echoes from the planetary cores".<ref name=":0" />
